questions.stem: A pedestrian struck by a car is in the trauma bay. Using the trauma note, fill in the bowtie: the likely cause of the shock in the middle, two priority interventions on the left and two parameters that show the response on the right.

condition.text: Hemorrhage from an unstable pelvic fracture

actions.text: Rock the pelvis again to confirm that it is unstable
Insert a urinary catheter at once to measure output
Give a large volume of crystalloid first

rationale.correct: An unstable pelvis with shock needs a binder and blood products.

perOption.c2: Heart rate is fast, not slow.
perOption.c3: Too early, and no hypoxemia or petechiae.
perOption.c4: No distended neck veins or muffled heart sounds.
perOption.a4: Blood at the meatus suggests a urethral injury.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize and act on pelvic fracture hemorrhage.

questions.stem: A client has a new long-leg cast after a tibia fracture. For each trend, choose the interpretation.

cells.text: Pink, pink, pale, pale and cool
Normal, normal, tingling, numb between the first and second toes

options.text: Rising pain out of proportion; report now
Expected after a fracture
Needs a stronger opioid only
Worsening perfusion
Normal variation
Improving
Nerve compression
From the opioid
Normal after casting

rationale.correct: Rising pain, pallor and numbness under a cast mean compartment syndrome; the cast may need bivalving.

perOption.b3:b: Opioids do not cause focal numbness.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse receives handoff on four orthopedic trauma clients at 0700. After handoff, which client should the nurse assess first?

options.text: A client 1 day after a total knee replacement who rates pain 6 out of 10 and wants the next dose of oxycodone
A client 2 days after a femur fracture who is newly confused with an SpO2 of 88%
A client in a cast who reports itching under the cast and asks for a coat hanger
A client after hip surgery whose drain has 150 mL of blood since the last shift

rationale.correct: New confusion with hypoxemia after a long-bone fracture is the priority.

perOption.a: Needs pain relief soon, but is stable.
perOption.b: Possible fat embolism; hypoxemia is the most urgent.
perOption.d: Within expected limits; check after the hypoxic client.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: On an infectious disease unit, which tasks can the RN delegate to the UAP? Select all that apply.

options.text: Take vital signs on a client in contact precautions for MRSA
Restock gowns and gloves outside isolation rooms
Bathe a client with C. difficile using soap and water for hand hygiene afterward
Assess a client with HIV for new oral lesions

questions.stem: The massive transfusion protocol is activated. Which actions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use a blood warmer
Check ionized calcium
Give tranexamic acid within 3 hours of injury
Monitor potassium
Give products cold straight from the fridge to save time
Wait for the full crossmatch before any blood

rationale.correct: Warm products, replace calcium, give TXA and monitor potassium.

perOption.f: Uncrossmatched O blood is used in emergencies.

options.text: Warm the client with a forced-air blanket
Give calcium as prescribed

questions.stem: After a splenectomy, for each statement or finding at discharge, indicate whether it shows understanding or progress, or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Hemoglobin stable at 9.8 g/dL for 48 hours
"I'll get the pneumococcal, meningococcal and Hib vaccines."
"A fever is no big deal now, I can wait a few days."
"I'll wear a medical alert bracelet."
Platelets 820,000/mm3 on day 5

rationale.correct: After splenectomy, vaccines and urgent care for fever are essential.

perOption.r3:c1: Overwhelming infection risk; seek care at once.
perOption.r3:c2: Overwhelming infection risk; seek care at once.
perOption.r5:c1: Reactive thrombocytosis; clot risk is reviewed.
perOption.r5:c2: Reactive thrombocytosis; clot risk is reviewed.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that define heat stroke.

rationale.correct: A core temperature above 40 C with altered mental status is heat stroke.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it fits heat exhaustion or heat stroke.

rows.text: Temperature 39 C with normal mental status
Confusion or seizures
Heavy sweating, nausea and headache with a clear mind
Temperature above 40 C with combative behavior

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

options.text: cooling to below 39 C within 30 minutes

antipyretics
oral fluids only

perOption.b1:c: Do not work in heat stroke.

questions.stem: Which actions should the nurse include during cooling? Select all that apply.

options.text: Monitor rectal temperature continuously
Remove from the water at about 38.6 to 39 C
Protect the airway and watch for seizures
Give acetaminophen to bring the temperature down
Cool until the temperature reaches 35 C

rationale.correct: Continuous core temperature, stop at 39 C and protect the airway.

rows.text: "I'll return to running gradually after my doctor clears me."

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: This client needs {{b1}}, and the nurse should expect {{b2}} as rewarming proceeds.

options.text: active internal rewarming such as warmed IV fluids and warmed humidified oxygen
only a blanket
a hot bath
rubbing the limbs
hypotension as vessels dilate (rewarming shock)
rising heart rate requiring beta blockers
permanent bradycardia
hypertension

rationale.correct: Active internal rewarming with fluids ready for rewarming shock.

perOption.b1:b: Passive rewarming is for mild cases.

Treat the low glucose

questions.stem: During transfer, the client becomes pulseless and the monitor shows ventricular fibrillation. The core temperature is 29.6 C. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Start high-quality CPR
Defibrillate once as per protocol
Continue active rewarming during CPR
Stop resuscitation after 10 minutes because the client is cold
Give repeated epinephrine every 3 minutes as at normal temperature

rationale.correct: CPR, one shock and continued rewarming; drugs are limited until warmer.

perOption.d: Not dead until warm and dead.
perOption.e: Drugs are held or spaced until warmer.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care
